What Democrats Are Saying About The Raid On Ilhan Omar’s Home, And Why They Call It An Attempt To Influence Midterms

By Christopher Rhodes • Oct 13, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:57
Instaread

The Trump administration sent federal agents to raid the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota) early Monday morning. The action, less than a month before Election Day, is being condemned by Democrats as an attempt to influence the midterm elections, and it is being viewed by many as an abuse of power against the outspoken congresswoman who has often been a target of the president and his allies.

Raid of Rep. Omar’s residence condemned by congresswoman, Democratic colleagues

Fox News reported that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative wing of the Department of Homeland Security, executed a search warrant at Rep. Omar’s Washington, D.C., residence at around 6 a.m. Monday. “Today in the Washington, D.C., area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice,” a DOJ spokesperson wrote to Fox. “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation,” the statement said. Trump administration officials, including border czar Tom Homan, had previously claimed that Omar was the subject of an unspecified criminal investigation, and the DOJ has described the investigation behind Monday’s search as “criminal” in nature, and sources have informed Fox that the investigation is focused on the possibility of immigration fraud relating to immigration paperwork that Omar’s father, now deceased, filled out when he brought his family to the United States; the congresswoman, who was born in Somalia, was a child when her family came to the U.S. as refugees.

News of the raid quickly outraged Democrats, who have characterized it as an abuse of power meant to impact the upcoming midterm elections. Omar described the raid as “an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” arguing that “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns.” Despite the attempt at “political intimidation,” Omar vowed, “I will not be silenced.”

Other Democrats quickly rallied to her side. The Congressional Black Caucus described the raid as a “sham” that was meant to “manufacture an appearance of wrongdoing on the eve of the midterm elections, without any apparent legal basis.”

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) issued a statement saying the raid was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries.”

Rep. Rashida Tlaib, who was elected alongside Omar in 2018 as the first Muslim women to serve in Congress, posted, “DHS raiding a member of congress’s home is exactly what a fascist police state does” and declared, “I stand with Ilhan.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani posted that Omar was being targeted “for the offense of disagreeing with the White House.” Mamdani added, “The path to citizenship should not be weaponized against anyone, including Rep. Ilhan Omar, a naturalized American who swore an oath to this country — the same one that I took.”

Trump continues bigoted attacks against Omar and others

Rep. Omar has frequently been the target of right-wing smears and conspiracy theories. President Trump has often targeted Omar and the Somali community of Minnesota with racist, xenophobic and Islamophobic rhetoric. Omar has described Trump’s preoccupation with her as an “obsession.” Many pointed to Trump’s demonization of Omar after the congresswoman was physically attacked by a man who doused her with a foul-smelling liquid as she spoke at a public town hall event.

The Trump administration, meanwhile, has repeatedly used the power of the federal government against the president’s political foes, including questionable criminal indictments against New York Attorney General Letitia James and former FBI Director James Comey, accusations of mortgage fraud against Federal Reserve Board member Lisa Cook, and threats of FCC “rebuke or punishment” against Meet the Press host Kristen Welker. After Monday’s raid, Trump continued to attack Omar, telling reporters, “I’ve always found her to be totally crooked, personally,” and calling her “a terrible person.” Trump denied he was responsible for the raid, claiming, “I have nothing to do with it.”

Trump again spoke about the raid at a Monday night campaign rally in Youngstown, Ohio, attacking Omar’s Somali heritage and mocking her “Constitutional right,” while also falsely labeling Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan as “a jihadist” and endorsing the GOP candidate in that race. “The Republican Party, we believe that Somalia bandits, third world gangs and jihadist sympathizers do not belong in Ohio, they don’t belong in America,” Trump declared to an applauding crowd. “Better get them the hell out of here.”

Trump’s attacks against American citizens like Omar and El-Sayed are disturbing, and the raid against Omar’s residence demonstrates that the president’s rhetoric is being backed by actions from his administration. As the investigation against the congresswoman proceeds amid Republican accusations against Rep. Omar, her family and her community, Omar and her allies continue to condemn Trump and his administration and point to the early-morning raid as the latest example of weaponizing the criminal justice system against the president’s opponents.
